what_it_does: Cloud providers let multiple customers share the same field-programmable gate array (FPGA) — a chip whose internal wiring can be reconfigured after manufacture. A known security risk is that a malicious tenant can detect what a neighboring tenant is doing by watching tiny fluctuations in the chip's power supply voltage — a 'power side-channel attack'. Existing attacks use custom-built sensor circuits, but FPGAs also contain abundant fixed-function DSP (digital signal processing) blocks, normally used to accelerate math, that have so far not been weaponized as sensors. LeakyDSP shows that DSP blocks can be deliberately misconfigured to act as voltage sensors, picking up fine-grained power fluctuations caused by a co-resident tenant's activity. This reveals a new hardware attack surface that defenders and cloud providers must account for when designing isolation policies, based on the abstract.
